title: Integrating network pharmacology and experimental validation to uncover the mechanisms of Ganoderma lucidum in ameliorating neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease.
authors: Sheng, Feiya; Yu, Jia-Mei; Yang, Qiao; Jipei, Rigu; Xie, Wen-Qi; Zhan, Gu; Zhang, Yan; Zhang, Le-Le
journal: The Journal of pharmacy and pharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文用网络药理学和分子对接研究灵芝抗神经炎症机制，虽涉及分子对接但对象为药物-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法聚焦TF-DNA，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to explore the anti-neuroinflammatory mechanism of Ganoderma lucidum against Alzheimer's disease (AD) using network pharmacology and molecular docking, and verify its neuroprotective and anti-neuroinflammatory effects in Abeta1-42-induced AD mice. METHODS: Common targets were screened and analyzed by KEGG/GO enrichment. Core targets were evaluated by molecular docking and dynamics simulation. Abeta1-42-induced AD mice and LPS-stimulated macrophages were used. Cognitive function, Abeta deposition, tau phosphorylation, and inflammatory gene expression were measured. KEY FINDINGS: Network analysis highlighted inflammation-related pathways. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed stable binding between active components and targets like STAT1, STAT3, JAK2, and TNF. In vivo, G. lucidum extract suppressed abnormal activation of microglia and astrocytes, and reduced pro-inflammatory factors. Following G. lucidum administration, mRNA levels of Jak2 and Stat1 in hippocampal tissue were significantly reduced, suggesting potential regulation of neuroinflammation via the JAK2/STAT1 pathway. Concurrently, G. lucidum down-regulated transcription of key subunits (Ncstn, Aph-1, Pen-2) in the gamma-secretase complex, thereby reducing Abeta1-42 production. In vitro experiments similarly confirmed G. lucidum's ability to inhibit LPS-induced IL-6 and TNF-alpha release from macrophages. CONCLUSIONS: Ganoderma lucidum extract alleviates neuroinflammation in AD models, providing experimental evidence for its potential application in AD prevention or therapy.
abstract_zh: 目的：本研究旨在通过网络药理学和分子对接技术，探讨灵芝（Ganoderma lucidum）抗阿尔茨海默病（AD）的神经炎症机制，并在Abeta1-42诱导的AD小鼠中验证其神经保护和抗神经炎症作用。方法：通过KEGG/GO富集分析筛选并分析共同靶点。通过分子对接和动力学模拟评估核心靶点。使用Abeta1-42诱导的AD小鼠和LPS刺激的巨噬细胞。测量认知功能、Abeta沉积、tau磷酸化和炎症基因表达。主要发现：网络分析突出了炎症相关通路。分子动力学模拟确认了活性成分与STAT1、STAT3、JAK2和TNF等靶点之间的稳定结合。在体内实验中，灵芝提取物抑制了小胶质细胞和星形胶质细胞的异常激活，并减少了促炎因子。灵芝给药后，海马组织中Jak2和Stat1的mRNA水平显著降低，提示其可能通过JAK2/STAT1通路调节神经炎症。同时，灵芝下调了γ-分泌酶复合物关键亚基（Ncstn、Aph-1、Pen-2）的转录，从而减少Abeta1-42的产生。体外实验同样证实了灵芝抑制LPS诱导的巨噬细胞释放IL-6和TNF-alpha的能力。结论：灵芝提取物缓解了AD模型中的神经炎症，为其在AD预防或治疗中的潜在应用提供了实验证据。
